Report_ID: Death or BPD at 36 weeks' postmenstrual age
Title: Two Doses of Early Intravenous Dexamethasone for the Prevention of Bronchopulmonary Dysplasia in Babies with Respiratory Distress Syndrome
Author: Sanders RJ, Cox C, Phelps DL, Sinkin RA
Comment: Death-or-BPD events computed as the complement of the paper's reported 'Survival without BPD' counts using the randomised denominators: dexamethasone 19−13=6, placebo 21−9=12. The paper does not report death-or-BPD directly, nor a risk ratio.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Dexamethasone (two i.v. doses of 0.5 mg/kg birth weight, first at 12-18 h of age; cumulative 1 mg/kg)') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Participant type: Ventilated premature infants <30 wk gestation with surfactant-treated RDS
Recruitment source: University of Rochester neonatal intensive care unit, Strong Children's Medical Center

Outcome variable: Death or BPD at 36 weeks' postmenstrual age
outcome_family: Death or bronchopulmonary dysplasia at 36 weeks' postmenstrual age
effect_direction: Favours dexamethasone (6/19 = 32% vs 12/21 = 57% dead or with BPD)

Report_ID: Death or bronchopulmonary dysplasia at 36 weeks' postmenstrual age (paper reports BPD incidence; deaths reported separately and not combined)
Title: Nebulized pentoxifylline for prevention of bronchopulmonary dysplasia in very low birth weight infants: A pilot clinical study
Author: Lauterbach R, Szymura-Oleksiak J, Pawlik D, Warchoł J, Lisowska-Miszczyk I, Rytlewski K
Comment: The paper does NOT report a combined 'death or BPD' outcome. These intention-to-treat counts (16/50 DX, 21/50 placebo) are BPD cases only; deaths before BPD diagnosis (12 in DX group, 12 in placebo group) are reported separately and were NOT added, so the combined outcome cannot be constructed verbatim. The paper's own effect estimate (OR 0.39, 95% CI 0.14–1.14, p=0.07; difference in risk 23%) refers to the analysed subset (BPD in 12/33 DX vs 16/27 placebo), not to these ITT counts, so it was not entered in the numeric OR fields to avoid mixing denominators. Also note 3 placebo infants withdrew consent, and dexamethasone courses (1.5 mg/kg per 3-day course) were repeated every 7 days, so cumulative dose may exceed 2 mg/kg in some infants.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Intravenous dexamethasone (DX) 0.25 mg/kg every 12 h for 3 consecutive days from day 4 of life, courses repeated every 7 days') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False); excluded by outcome classification: does not match the requested outcome/timepoint (meta_analysis_candidate=False)
Participant type: Very low birth weight preterm infants (<1500 g; mean gestational age ~28.5 weeks) requiring oxygen on the fourth day of life
Recruitment source: Neonatal intensive care unit, Department of Neonatology, Jagiellonian University Medical College, Kraków, Poland (Jan 2000 – Sep 2003)
Outcome measurement: Number of infants with BPD (oxygen dependency at 36 weeks PMA) out of number randomised per arm (intention-to-treat analysis)
Outcome variable: Death or bronchopulmonary dysplasia at 36 weeks' postmenstrual age (paper reports BPD incidence; deaths reported separately and not combined)
additional_group_ns: Nebulized pentoxifylline (PTX) arm excluded per synthesis plan: 50 randomised, 37 analysed, BPD in 14/50 (ITT) and 12/37 (analysed)
outcome_family: Death or bronchopulmonary dysplasia at 36 weeks' postmenstrual age
effect_direction: Favours dexamethasone on BPD alone (16/50 vs 21/50); composite not reported

Title: Failure of early postnatal dexamethasone to prevent chronic lung disease in infants with respiratory distress syndrome

Participant type: Preterm infants with RDS, birthweight 500–2000 g, mean gestational age 29 weeks, <12 hours of age, surfactant-treated, mechanically ventilated

outcome_family: Death or bronchopulmonary dysplasia at 36 weeks' postmenstrual age

Comment: No P value, risk ratio or CI reported for the combined outcome (paper states only that it was 'comparable'). Comment: Events for 'death or CLD' were derived as the arithmetic complement of the paper's explicitly reported 'Survival without CLD' counts (118-83=35 dexamethasone; 123-71=52 placebo); denominators are the numbers randomised. Table 3 header states placebo n=122 but row denominators and the Methods state n=123.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Early dexamethasone (3-day tapering course, total 1.35 mg/kg, later 1.175 mg/kg, begun 24-48 h of life)') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)

Author: Tapia JL, Ramírez R, Cifuentes J, Fabres J, Hübner ME, Bancalari A, Mercado ME, Standen J, Escobar M
Comment: Combined death-or-BPD at 36 weeks is NOT reported directly by the paper. Events were summed per the synthesis plan from the paper's own Table II counts: placebo 18 deaths + 12 oxygen-dependent survivors at 36 wk = 30/54; dexamethasone 17 deaths + 3 oxygen-dependent survivors = 20/55. Recruitment source: four neonatology units in Chile, December 1, 1992 to June 30, 1995

Report_ID: Death or bronchopulmonary dysplasia at 36 weeks' postmenstrual age (composite)
Title: A single very early dexamethasone dose improves respiratory and cardiovascular adaptation in preterm infants
Author: Kopelman AE, Moise AA, Holbert D, Hegemier SE
Comment: Composite counts are DERIVED, not reported verbatim: deaths are explicit (10/37 dexamethasone; 5/33 control); BPD among survivors is reported only as percentages (22% of 27 survivors = 5.94 -> 6; 18% of 28 survivors = 5.04 -> 5). Composite = 10+6 = 16/37 and 5+5 = 10/33. Note the Discussion states BPD "occurred in just 6 (18%) of the control infants", which is inconsistent with 18% of 28 survivors (=5); if 6 control survivors had BPD the control composite would be 11/33. No risk ratio, odds ratio, or P value is reported by the paper for this composite.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Dexamethasone 0.2 mg/kg IV within 2 h of delivery') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Participant type: Inborn preterm infants <28 weeks' gestation requiring intermittent mandatory ventilation and arterial catheterization
Recruitment source: East Carolina University School of Medicine (Greenville, NC) and Baylor College of Medicine (Houston, TX) NICUs, Aug 1994 - Nov 1995
Outcome measurement: Number of infants who died plus number of surviving infants with a diagnosis of BPD (IMV or oxygen requirement) at 36 weeks' corrected gestational age, out of the number randomised
Outcome variable: Death or bronchopulmonary dysplasia at 36 weeks' postmenstrual age (composite)
outcome_family: Death or bronchopulmonary dysplasia at 36 weeks' postmenstrual age
effect_direction: Favours placebo (16/37 = 43% vs 10/33 = 30% dead or with BPD)
